subject: physics_2
question_text: What are the units of magnetic moment, magnetic induction and magnetic field?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are both STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: magnetic moment M is in ampere metre² (A·m²); magnetic induction B is in tesla (1 T = 1 Wb/m²; 1 gauss = 10⁻⁴ T); magnetic field intensity H is in ampere per metre (A/m) — the three units the book lists, checked against M = NiA, F = qvB and B = μ₀(H + M) in free space.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Moment and induction
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name both units with their symbols — A·m² for the moment, tesla for the induction.
steps.why: The unit of M follows from M = NiA — ampere times metre squared. The unit of B follows from F = qvB, and one tesla is one weber of flux through one square metre.
common_mistakes: Writing A·m for the moment. The area brings metre squared, so the unit is A·m².
Giving tesla for H. Tesla is the unit of the induction B, not of the field intensity H.

recall.must_convey: That magnetic moment is measured in ampere metre squared and magnetic induction in tesla or gauss.
accept: ampere metre squared for the moment
gauss is also a unit of induction

steps.memory_tip: M = NiA: ampere from the current, metre squared from the area — A·m².

steps.label: Magnetic field H

lines.text: M: A·m² · B: tesla (T) · H: A/m

steps.margin_note: Second mark. The magnetic field here means the field intensity H, and its unit is A/m.
steps.why: H comes from the current per unit length that produces the field (as inside a solenoid, H = nI), so its unit is ampere per metre — different from tesla, which measures B.
common_mistakes: Leaving this part out because B was already answered. The question asks three units, and H is the third.

recall.must_convey: That magnetic field intensity H is measured in ampere per metre.
accept: A per m for the field intensity
H is in ampere per metre

steps.memory_tip: Inside a solenoid H = nI — turns per metre times ampere, so ampere per metre.

insider_note: Three quantities are asked, so write three labelled unit lines — most students stop after tesla and lose the A/m mark.
